title: Calla and the Tiny Robot's Algorithm
markdown:
Calla was tidying among the towering bookshelves. Sunlight made dust motes dance. Her friend Sprig the mole, straw hat on, arranged leaves. They loved quiet days that turned remarkable.

A faint whirring tickled their ears. Peeking from under a giant atlas, something glowed. Calla nudged the book. “What’s this?”

There sat a robot no bigger than a teacup. Metal gleamed. Tiny lights blinked like friendly eyes. Bip-bip-wheee! It looked bewildered.

Sprig nudged his trowel. “Don’t worry, little friend.” The robot only wheee-bip-ed, a tiny sigh.

“He’s trying to tell us something.”

Dr Ada, the village inventor, bustled in. “Goodness me. Ah — Glitch. He must have zipped away from his charging station. Oops.”

Glitch’s lights blinked faster. Bip-bip-bip!

“He needs clear instructions to get home,” Ada said. “Step by step, like a recipe. You can’t dump all the ingredients in at once. A special list. An algorithm.”

Sprig wiggled his whiskers. “An algorithm?”

“Step-by-step directions for a robot. We’ll create one for Glitch.”

Calla grabbed a pencil. “First, he needs to move away from this atlas.” She drew an arrow. “Then where?”

Ada pointed. “Turn left at the end of that row.” A curved arrow.

Sprig scampered ahead. “Look! That blinking light — like his home symbol!”

“Brilliant. His charging station. Next step: go toward that symbol.” Calla drew another arrow.

Together they made cards: Move Forward. A left-turn arrow. The blinking symbol. A picture of the charging station.

“His algorithm,” Ada announced. “Step one: move forward. Step two: turn left. Step three: go toward the blinking symbol. Step four: you’re home.”

She placed the first card. Glitch blinked happily, beeeeep-ed, and rolled forward along the arrow. At the aisle’s end Calla held up the next card. He turned left. He hummed, lights fixed on the blinking symbol.

There it was. He rolled in with a happy wheeeeee-ding! Lights settled to a steady blue. Home.

“You did it, Glitch!” Calla and Sprig cheered.

Ada winked. “You created the algorithm. Big tasks into clear steps.” She did not need a jungle-expedition speech. The little robot, charging, was enough.

Calla stacked the cards in order, a recipe you could hold. Sprig’s hat had gone slightly sideways from the scampering. Calla wondered what else might need four honest steps — a row of beans, a shelf of books, a way home when you were only teacup-sized. Glitch’s blue light stayed steady. The atlas stayed shut. The next instruction, if they needed one, could wait.
characters: Calla (a farm helper), Sprig (a mole), Ada (an inventor)
author: StoryGen Community
